resources.string: The European PC DVD, as an .iso. It is unpacked on this device; nothing is uploaded.
The English v1.0.1 executable, bare or in a .zip. It is checked against the build this port was made from.

The game is read from plain files, so everything it needs must end up in real storage. The picker above already does that without any permission. Allowing all files access only adds two shortcuts: using an unpacked game folder where it lies, and installing to a folder of your choice. It grants access to the whole shared storage, so it is optional.
All files access not granted. Optional: the picker works without it.
All files access not granted. Tap to review the setting.
In the system screen, allow this app to manage all files, then come back. This screen checks again when you return.
This device has no All Files Access screen. Use the picker instead.
All files access needs Android 11 or newer. Use the picker instead.
This device has no folder picker. Use the disc image instead.
%1$s does not look like an unpacked Virtua Tennis 3 folder: it has no Resource folder.
Reading the game from %1$s. It is used where it lies: nothing is copied.
%1$s can be read but not written. The game keeps its settings and saves there, so it is copied into app storage instead.
%1$s cannot be read any more (a removed card, or a deleted folder). Pick the game folder again.
%1$s holds more than one folder with a Resource folder (%2$s). Pick the one that is the game data folder.
%1$s cannot be read. Pick the folder again.
Reading a folder outside app storage needs all files access. Grant it above, or copy the game in with the picker.
Folder chosen. Its files are copied into app storage while installing.
%1$s cannot be written, so its files are copied into app storage while installing.
That folder has no Resource folder, so it is not an unpacked Virtua Tennis 3 install. Pick the folder that holds Resource, or the folder that contains it.
That folder holds more than one folder with a Resource folder (%1$s). Pick the game data folder itself.
That folder could not be opened. Its permission may have been revoked: pick it again.
The folder chosen earlier is no longer accessible. Pick it again, or use the disc image.
There are no files in that folder.
VT3.exe found in the game folder: %1$s
No VT3.exe in that folder or the archive folders above it: select it in step 2.
Choosing another install folder needs all files access. Grant it above, or keep app storage.

The install folder cannot be inside the game folder. Choose app storage or another folder.
Nothing was installed. The game data is incomplete.
Nothing was chosen to install. Select the disc image or a game folder.
VT3.exe was not chosen. Select it, or pick the game folder that holds it.
Not enough free space: this install needs %1$s and only %2$s is free.
The installed game data cannot be read any more. Set it up again here: nothing else on this device was deleted.
%1$s has no Resource folder, so the game would not start. Nothing was kept.
Cannot clear the partial install at %1$s. Remove it, then try again.
Install cancelled. The partial copy was removed, and your own game folder was not touched.
An unpacked game folder needs no extra space. Unpacking the disc image needs about 4.5 GB.
Requires your own copy of Virtua Tennis 3. Unofficial fan port, not affiliated with SEGA.
Choose the disc image or a game folder to see what the install will need.
This folder is read where it lies: no copy and no extra space are needed.
This folder is copied into app storage: about %1$s free is needed.
This source is unpacked into app storage: about %1$s free is needed.
The game has not been installed yet.
The game folder %1$s is gone (a removed card, or a deleted folder).
%1$s no longer holds the game data (its Resource folder is missing).
The game image is missing from app storage. Run setup again to rebuild it.
The language of these screens: setup, the main menu, settings and diagnostics.
The game\'s own text and commentary come from the disc you installed. The European release carries English, French, German, Spanish and Italian; the game picks its language there.
Low, Medium and High are starting points chosen for this device; Auto follows the device; Custom keeps your own settings. Changing any option below switches the preset to Custom.
Native panel renders at the screen\'s own height. A lower height costs less GPU time and heat.
Renders at a percentage of the chosen height and scales up. Lower is cooler and faster.
Texture filtering for surfaces seen at an angle, such as the court. The thermal guard can lower it while the phone is hot.
Hor+ widescreen fill. Off restores the original 4:3 framing.
The game\'s variance shadow maps. Off is cheaper on the GPU and slightly flatter under the lights.
30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55 or 60 fps, or the panel\'s own rate. The limit is independent of the preset.
Frame pacing follows this limit: the renderer paces frames to it and asks the panel for the matching rate. Changing pacing never resets a graphics setting.
A compact panel during gameplay: frames per second, CPU temperature and battery temperature. Hidden in menus.
Compact is one line; expanded adds frame time and the thermal status.
Gradual, reversible steps when Android reports the phone is hot: lower anisotropy at once, a lower resolution on the next launch. Off keeps your settings fixed.
From Android\'s thermal service and this device\'s own tier.
Effective now: %1$s fps, height %2$s, anisotropy %3$s, scale %4$s%%
Graphics settings are read when the renderer starts, so this launches the game with them. Every setting is already saved; Back leaves without starting.
Go back to setup? The game data stays on this device; the next install can read a different folder or unpack the disc image again.
The touch pad, buttons and sticks drawn over the game on a phone.
On-screen controls stay visible even while a physical controller is connected, which is the way to ignore the pad and play on the glass.
Scales the whole on-screen layout, sticks included.
Lower keeps the court readable under the controls.
Draws the controls in one colour instead of the per-button accents.
A physical controller and keyboard are always supported; the on-screen controls hide themselves when one is used, unless the option above keeps them on.
Applied to the mixed game output on this device.
Silences the game\'s music and effects without stopping the mixer.
Audio runs on its own thread through AAudio, separate from the render thread; these settings do not change its buffering.
The port\'s Direct3D 9 translation runs on Vulkan on Android.
As advertised by the platform; the renderer selects its paths from these capabilities, not from the GPU brand.
The translated SPIR-V shaders, refreshed when the app is updated.
Available of total, as Android reports it.
Adds debug detail to the log. Off by default, so normal play is not flooded.
Logs the mixer once a second: underruns, stale blocks, ring occupancy.
Logs the renderer\'s frame-time histogram once a second.
These write to the same log as everything else. They cost time every second and are meant for a report, not for play.
Developer tools appear here when detailed logging is on.
Reset graphics to the device defaults
The folder holds Resource/ and the image was built from the supported VT3.exe.
Where a copied install goes; app storage unless changed.
Optional; the picker works without it.
Change game folder or disc image
The game data at %1$s is readable and complete enough to start. The VT3.exe image was verified when it was built.
Changing the source clears the install record only. Nothing in your own game folder is deleted, and an install that still validates can be kept.
This device has no file picker.
There is no earlier import to restore.
Imported packages removed. The system driver was not touched.
Nothing here writes outside the app\'s own storage, needs root, or changes a system partition. A driver package you import stays yours; none is bundled.
That file is not a usable driver package

string-array.item: A / Cross — top spin (flat shot when held with the stick centred)
Left stick — movement; the stick also drives the d-pad, so menus navigate
LB / RB — modifier for the advanced shots
Start — pause / open the game\'s main menu
Back / Select — the port\'s quick menu (on-screen controls, guide, settings)
Guide — the port\'s quick menu, on pads that report it

resources.string: The game and this screen write one log on this device: startup, the game engine, the installer, storage, Vulkan, frame times, audio, input and the Android lifecycle. Nothing is uploaded. A report is a plain .txt file you can read, save or share.
Detailed logging (adds debug detail; turn off when done)

Version %1$s
Log size %2$s (%3$s entries, %4$s dropped)
Last report %5$s
Last error: %6$s

The report contains the app version, device model and Android version, the install state, graphics and frame statistics, audio diagnostics, lifecycle events and the error history. It never contains file contents, account details or a location. Clearing logs removes only the log files and crash records, never the game.
This device has no document picker, so the report cannot be saved.
No report has been saved yet.
No app on this device can open a text file.
Delete the log files, the last-error record and crash records on this device? The game and its data are not touched.
Logs cleared. The game data was not touched.
Save cancelled: no file was written.
Report saved and verified: %1$d bytes, readable.
The report could not be saved: %1$s
Keeps the overlay clear of the on-screen controls
Frame limit, resolution, render scale, anisotropy, shadows and widescreen are read when a match starts: a change applies to the next match, including one started after returning to the main menu.
